title: SIM Card for Tourists in India: Local SIM, eSIM and What Works Where
seo_title: SIM Card in India for Tourists: SIM, eSIM & Coverage
seo_desc: Can tourists get a SIM card in India? Documents, how long activation takes, local SIM vs travel eSIM, and why Kashmir, Ladakh and the mountains differ.
label: SIM cards & eSIM for visitors
blurb: Documents, activation, eSIM vs local SIM, and signal in the mountains
sub: A plain-English guide for visitors from the US, UK, Europe, Australia and Canada: who can get an Indian SIM, the documents the shop will ask for, how long activation takes, when a travel eSIM is easier — and the two things most guides miss: Kashmir and Ladakh rules, and no signal in the high mountains. Written by a travel company in Himachal that sells no SIM cards.
hero_alt: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, the rooftops of Jaisalmer, the Manali valley, a shikara on Dal Lake in Srinagar and the Taj Mahal — places where visitors need a working phone
q: Can tourists buy a SIM card in India?
answer: Yes. Foreign visitors can get an Indian prepaid SIM from an operator's store or counter with their passport, a valid Indian visa, a passport photo and a local address such as a hotel or tour operator. Activation can take from a few hours to a day or two, and a tourist connection runs for up to 3 months. For Kashmir and Ladakh, only postpaid connections from other states work.

sections.h2: Before you read: what this page is
sections.text: This page is general information, checked 27 Oct 2026. We don't sell SIM cards or eSIMs and we don't recommend any provider. Rules and plans change — confirm with the operator before you buy.

sections.h2: Three ways to have a phone in India
sections.lead: Most visitors pick one of these. Which is best depends on how long you stay, where you go and whether you need an Indian number.
head: Option
How it works
Good to know
rows: Bought in India from an operator's own store or counter, with in-person ID checks
Gives you an Indian number for calls, messages and one-time passwords; activation is not instant; up to 3 months per connection
Travel eSIM bought before you fly
A data plan from an international eSIM seller, installed on your phone at home
Works from landing if your phone supports eSIM; usually data only, no Indian number; check the plan covers India
Simplest; check the daily cost with your operator before you go
sections.note: An Indian eSIM from an Indian operator usually still needs the same in-person ID check, and online self-activation generally needs an Indian number to receive a one-time password — so first-time visitors usually can't set one up from home.

sections.h2: What the shop will ask for
sections.lead: These are the documents listed by COAI, the association of India's mobile operators, for international visitors.
items: Passport
The original, plus a photocopy of the passport pages with your valid Indian visa.
Indian visa
Your visa or e-Visa. Apply yourself at the official site indianvisaonline.gov.in; beware look-alike sites that charge extra. We are not a visa agency.
A passport-size colour photo
A printed photo, not a scan. Carry two in case.
A local address
The address of a local reference — it may be your tour operator — or, without one, where you're staying, such as your hotel. Keep your first hotel booking handy.
The application form
The shop gives you a form to fill in and sign. Keep the receipt it hands back — you may need its details to activate the SIM.
sections.note: Since a Department of Telecommunications order of 31 July 2024, a one-time password on a local Indian number is optional for foreign nationals; operators may send it to your email instead.

sections.h2: How long it takes, and how long it lasts
items: Not instant

COAI explains that the SIM is issued first but can't make or receive calls until the operator finishes verification — a wait that can run from a few hours to a day or two. Buy it on day one, not on the morning you need it.
Up to 3 months
For foreign tourists a connection must not run past your visa, and cannot be longer than 3 months at a time, even if your visa is longer.
Buy from the operator

Use an operator's own store or counter. Some international airports have operator counters in the arrivals area; otherwise ask your hotel for the nearest official store. Avoid street stalls, which may sell SIMs registered to someone else.
Keep your home SIM
Many phones take two SIMs, or one SIM plus an eSIM — keep your home number for bank messages and use the Indian one for data and local calls.

sections.h2: Kashmir and Ladakh: the prepaid rule
paras: Prepaid SIMs from other parts of India don't work in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh; postpaid connections do. Confirm with the operator before you go. This is a long-standing telecom licence condition for these border areas, so a prepaid SIM bought in Delhi will stop working when you arrive in Srinagar or Leh.

If your trip includes Kashmir or Ladakh, plan for it: a travel eSIM or roaming on your home SIM, or a connection issued inside the region. We tell you in your plan which days this affects. For Kashmir, also check current travel advice — the UK and US governments both advise against travel to most of Jammu & Kashmir; see our Kashmir seasons page for the dated details.

sections.h2: No signal in the high mountains — and no satellite phones
sections.lead: Himachal, Spiti, Ladakh and Uttarakhand are some of the best places in India — and some of the worst for phone signal.
items: Expect gaps
The UK Foreign Office: "You are extremely unlikely to have a phone signal in the mountains, so make sure your accommodation provider registers your whereabouts using the online C-form."
Satellite phones are illegal

"It is illegal to possess and operate satellite phones and GPS devices in India without a licence." "You can be fined or arrested for possession of these devices without permission" (UK Foreign Office, advice updated 7 Oct 2026). Leave them at home.
Weather and protests
The same advice notes that mobile networks and internet may be disrupted during demonstrations, and that monsoon storms can cut telephone lines, internet and power.
Download before you go
Save offline maps, your hotel list and booking details on your phone before mountain days, so you aren't relying on signal.

sections.h2: How we keep you in touch on the road
items: A plan that shows signal gaps
Your day-by-day plan tells you which road days and overnight stops are in the high mountains or in Kashmir and Ladakh, so you know when to expect no signal.
Your driver's details first
Your driver's name, photo and car number are shared with you before the trip, so you know who is meeting you even before your Indian SIM works.
Our office by WhatsApp
Reach us on +91 70874 88961 by call or WhatsApp before and during your trip — WhatsApp works on hotel Wi-Fi too.
In an emergency
Dial 112, India's national emergency number (UK Foreign Office). Save your embassy's number and your insurer's 24-hour line before you travel — see our travel insurance checklist.

faqs: Can tourists buy a SIM card in India?

Yes. Foreign visitors can get an Indian connection from an operator's store or counter with a passport, valid Indian visa, a passport-size photo and a local address such as a hotel or tour operator (COAI).
What documents do I need for an Indian SIM card?
Your original passport and a photocopy with the visa page, a printed passport-size colour photo, a local address (hotel or tour operator) and the signed application form the shop gives you.
Can I get an Indian eSIM as a tourist?

Indian operators offer eSIMs, but they usually need the same in-person ID check, and online self-activation generally needs an Indian number. A travel eSIM bought before you fly is the easier eSIM option for most visitors.
How long does SIM activation take in India?
It is not instant. The SIM can't make or receive calls until the operator finishes verification, which can take from a few hours to a day or two. Buy it on your first day.
How long is a tourist SIM card valid in India?
For foreign tourists a connection must not run past the visa and cannot be longer than 3 months at a time, even with a longer visa (COAI).
Will my SIM work in Kashmir and Ladakh?

Prepaid SIMs from other parts of India don't work in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh; postpaid connections do. Confirm with the operator before you go. Roaming on your home SIM or a travel eSIM are alternatives.
Is there phone signal in the Himalaya?
Often not. The UK Foreign Office says you are extremely unlikely to have a phone signal in the mountains. Download offline maps and share your plan before mountain days.
Can I bring a satellite phone to India?
No, not without a licence. The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to possess and operate satellite phones and GPS devices in India without a licence, and you can be fined or arrested.
